title: Trunk bending stiffness in upright passive flexion while holding 3.5-7 kg loads (active muscle)
condition: holding 3.5 or 7 kg below/above the harness rod (ACTIVE muscle, increased EMG)

quantity.name: average trunk bending stiffness Kb = (ME - MS)/(thetaE - thetaS)
quantity.definition: secant stiffness over each interval (0-10% and quartiles) of the imposed flexion (70% of active lumbar range) during the flexion phase; moment about S1 from the harness-rod load cell

source.authors: Shojaei I, Suri C, van Dieen JH, Bazrgari B
source.sample: 20 asymptomatic young adults, gender-balanced (10 M: 178.0 (6.2) cm, 78.9 (12.0) kg, BMI 24.8; 10 F: 164.7 (5.1) cm, 67.1 (7.0) kg, BMI 24.7), age 18-30 y

protocol.summary: Rigid metal frame: pelvis/legs on a platform rotated about the S1 level (height adjusted per subject), thorax restrained at the harness-connecting rod with inline load cell; legs rotated to 70% of each subject's active lumbar flexion range (from a free bending test with IMUs on T10 and S1) and returned. Moment = rod force x distance from harness to platform axis (S1). Six tests: 2 without hand load (baseline) and 4 holding 3.5 or 7 kg at a fixed horizontal distance below or above the rod (equilibrium vs stability demand). EMG (4 back, 4 abdominal sites) in microvolts.
how_to_simulate: Upright model, thorax fixed at the harness level, pelvis+legs rotated about S1 to 70% of the model's lumbar flexion range

Hold 3.5 or 7 kg in the hands at a fixed horizontal distance in front of the lower back with muscle activation solved for equilibrium/stability (e.g. stability-constrained optimisation or EMG-driven), then compute trunk stiffness including active muscle short-range stiffness
Compute secant stiffness over 0-10% and each quartile of the imposed range and compare

subject_model.source: Methods 2.1 (mean of male and female means; derived)

protocol.notes: ACTIVE: includes muscle stiffness from load-holding co-activation; never pool with passive tests. Same lab/apparatus as Shojaei 2016 and Toosizadeh 2012.
